Can we move from Artificial Intelligence to Planetary Intelligence?

As we mark World Environment Day, this may be one of the most important questions of our time.
When World Environment Day was established in 1973, it carried the slogan "Only One Earth." More than 50 years later, that message feels more relevant than ever.

Today, the world is navigating profound transformations. Rising geopolitical tensions are reshaping energy security, while rapid advances in digitalization and artificial intelligence are accelerating demand for electricity and critical resources.
 
Yet amid these challenges, there are reasons for optimism. Despite the impacts of conflicts in the Middle East, global energy investment is expected to increase by 5%, reaching USD 3.4 trillion in 2026.
 
2025 also marked a historic milestone: for the first time, renewable energy generated more electricity globally than coal. Solar power expanded more rapidly in 2025 than any energy source in history.
 
The opportunity is significant. A just energy transition could reduce energy import bills by 38%, create 14 million green jobs, and lift 45 million people out of energy poverty by 2035.
 
At the same time, data centres already account for around 2% of global electricity demand and are projected to more than double their consumption by 2030. Yet the same technologies driving this growth can become part of the solution. AI-enabled grid management and digital twins are already improving renewable energy integration by 20–30%, helping build more flexible and efficient energy systems. More than half of critical mineral projects overlap with or are located near Indigenous Peoples' lands. 
 
But intelligence alone is not enough. The challenge is how we apply it.
 
Planetary Intelligence means using innovation not only to optimize economies, but also to better understand and manage the interconnected relationship between energy, nature, communities, and development. It means recognizing that healthy ecosystems, forests, wetlands, and oceans are as critical to our future as data centres, grids, and digital infrastructure. Nature-based solutions alone could provide up to one-third of the climate mitigation needed by 2030 while strengthening resilience and protecting livelihoods.
 
There is only one Earth. If we choose the right path, the journey from Artificial Intelligence to Planetary Intelligence may become one of the defining opportunities of our generation.
